fatal.title: rollback deletes files outside the target via an unvalidated install_path taken from the install receipt
fatal.location: tools/v0_incremental_package.py:1765-1809 (command_rollback precheck and removal loop); missing validation compared with install-side checks at tools/v0_incremental_package.py:1025-1039
fatal.trigger: the JSON install receipt handed to `rollback` is edited so that owned.files[0].install_path is a relative path that escapes the target (e.g. ../../victim.txt) and owned.files[0].sha256 is the sha256 of a file outside the target
fatal.expected: rollback refuses the receipt (non-zero exit, stable error code) and deletes nothing outside the target
fatal.actual: rollback exits 0 with status OK, reports removed_files[0] = "../../victim.txt" and deletes the out-of-target file
fatal.contract_clause: stage-packet-preparation-b.md: rollback binds session and installed hashes, removes only this round owned files/directories, never recursively deletes non-owned files

fatal.title: rollback performs an unvalidated recursive delete of any directory named by the receipt's staging.path
fatal.trigger: the install receipt's staging.path field is edited to point at any directory outside the target
fatal.expected: rollback refuses the receipt and only ever touches a staging directory it created inside the recorded sandbox parent
fatal.actual: rollback calls shutil.rmtree(staging, ignore_errors=True) on the attacker-chosen directory, destroys it, and still exits 0 with status OK and staging_removed=true; the report note still claims "only files owned by this install session were removed"
fatal.contract_clause: stage-packet-preparation-b.md: rollback must not modify external original files; unverified receipt fields must not be able to delete non-owned content

major.title: rollback binds the target by basename only, so a same-named directory in a different sandbox is deleted
major.location: tools/v0_incremental_package.py:1738-1756 (target selection and name-only comparison); the receipt's sandbox_parent is never re-checked and the sandbox marker is never re-verified in rollback
major.trigger: install into sandbox A / target X, then run `rollback --receipt <A receipt> --target <sandbox B>/X` where B is a different sandbox parent
major.expected: rollback refuses because the target is not the sandbox/session recorded in the receipt
major.actual: rollback exits 0 with status OK and deletes 29 files in sandbox B (28 owned + 1 user file); the receipt's sandbox_parent, session_id and sandbox marker are ignored
major.contract_clause: stage-packet-preparation-b.md: rollback binds session and installed hashes; it must not allow cross-target deletion merely because the target name matches

minor.title: Windows name-normalisation collisions (trailing dot, trailing space) are not rejected
minor.trigger: a package contains both payload/.../zz.py and payload/.../zz.py. with a manifest that declares both

minor.severity_note: POSIX sandbox only; the post-install hash re-check fails safe on Windows when the two members differ, so this is a portability gap rather than a proven data-loss path

re-run the candidate test suite plus this independent probe set against the corrected candidate, then re-run the four-step chain once and re-verify cleanup
